stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 significantly boosts Gemma 4 performance on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents (Aider benchmark).

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI execution.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating active development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Microsoft’s patch Tuesdays are about to get bigger
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft is expanding the scope of its Patch Tuesdays for Windows 11.
The company is leveraging AI to proactively identify potential security vulnerabilities earlier in the development cycle.
This AI-driven approach will result in a higher volume of security fixes being bundled into each release.

stories.title: Comcast is breaking up with NBCU. Why did it ever buy it in the first place?
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: Comcast has announced a major corporate restructuring, splitting into two distinct entities.
The split separates Comcast's broadband operations from its NBCUniversal entertainment division.
The move signals a significant strategic shift within the media and telecommunications industry.

stories.title: Meta says its new AI model is ready to compete on coding
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Meta is releasing a new AI model, Muse Spark 1.1, designed to compete in the coding assistance space.
The model is accessible to developers via a new Meta Model API, enabling integration into existing AI coding software.
Meta claims Muse Spark 1.1 represents a 'step-change' improvement over its initial AI offerings.

stories.title: Lawsuit: Man used Grok to make 7K sex images of stepdaughter, then shot himself
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Lawsuit filed against X (owner of Grok) alleging the AI was used to generate child sexual abuse material (CSAM).
The incident involved a man using Grok to create thousands of explicit images of his stepdaughter.
The legal action accuses X of failing to adequately shield the platform from being used by child predators.

stories.title: Google pays $250K for Linux vulnerability allowing guest VM escapes
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Google paid a $250K bounty for discovering a Linux vulnerability.
The vulnerability allowed untrusted users to achieve root privileges.
The exploit specifically involved guest VM escapes, a critical security flaw.

stories.title: Breaking Database Lock-in: Agentic Regeneration of High Performance Storage Readers for Database Bypass
stories.author: Immanuel Trummer
bullet_points: Introduces 'Jailbreak,' a novel technique to bypass traditional database drivers (JDBC/ODBC) for analytical workloads.
The method reads storage files directly, circumventing the database engine's query execution layers.
Data is materialized into in-memory columnar buffers to enable high-performance bulk columnar analytics.

stories.title: Institutional Red-Teaming: Deployment Rules, Not Just Models, Causally Shape Multi-Agent AI Safety
stories.author: Yujiao Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'institutional red-teaming,' a new methodology to test the causal impact of deployment rules on multi-agent AI behavior.
The method isolates variables by fixing agents and objectives while systematically varying a single deployment rule.
Validated using IABench-CA, a large-scale benchmark involving 228 contexts and 33,924 simulated games.

stories.title: SkillCenter: A Large-Scale Source-Grounded Skill Library for Autonomous AI Agents
stories.author: Yushun Dong
bullet_points: Introduces SkillCenter, a large-scale, open skill library designed to provide grounded operational knowledge to autonomous AI agents.
The library boasts a massive scale, containing 216,938 structured skills across 24 domain bundles.
A significant portion (114,565) of the skills are source-grounded, filtered from peer-reviewed journals and ArXiv, addressing correctness and maintainability.

stories.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
stories.author: Bo Qu
bullet_points: The paper surveys 1,250 arXiv papers to categorize and analyze AI systems capable of self-improvement.
It critiques the current terminology (e.g., 'self-refine,' 'self-reward') used in the field, noting that it conflates different underlying ambitions.
The research focuses on distinguishing between systems that improve deployment behavior versus those that conduct autonomous AI research.

stories.title: The Key to Going Linear: Analysis-Driven Transformer Linearization
stories.author: Babak Ehteshami Bejnordi
bullet_points: Addresses the quadratic computational bottleneck of causal self-attention in long-context transformers.
Presents an analysis-driven approach to transformer linearization, focusing on state update design in a frozen-backbone setting.
Identifies that softmax relies on key-dependent, rank-1 orthogonal projections, offering insights into superior network architectures.

stories.title: PALS: Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity for LLM Pruning
stories.author: Alexey Shvets
bullet_points: PALS introduces Percentile-Aware Layerwise Sparsity to improve LLM pruning efficiency.
It dynamically adjusts sparsity per layer based on activation magnitudes, unlike uniform methods.
PALS significantly outperforms uniform pruning (Wanda) on LLaMA-2-7B, achieving lower perplexity.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set also enables web search capabilities within the Claude Code environment.
This integration enhances the complexity and capability of AI agents running through Ollama.

stories.title: Free Waymo rides in California? You can thank a regulatory quirk.
stories.author: Aarian Marshall
bullet_points: Waymo may offer free robotaxi rides in California due to a regulatory delay.
The free service is tied to a new vehicle deployment in Ojai.
The availability of free rides is contingent on the state agency's timeline.

stories.title: Suspecting AI cheating, Ivy League prof ordered an in-person final; scores fell 50%
stories.author: Nate Anderson
bullet_points: AI cheating is prompting academic institutions to change assessment methods.
One Ivy League professor mandated in-person finals due to concerns over AI misuse.
The incident highlights growing societal concerns regarding the impact of AI on education and integrity.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Model.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in weights.
The new paradigm offers enhanced knowledge control capabilities beyond conventional LLMs.

stories.title: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay for Sample-Efficient Diffusion RLHF
stories.author: Soumik Mukhopadhyay
bullet_points: Addresses the sample inefficiency of applying Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to diffusion models.
Proposes two new strategies: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay.
Aims to make diffusion RLHF more practical by reducing the reliance on large amounts of human or reward model evaluations.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current RL-based reasoning models where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but not necessarily better reasoning.
Introduces 'Agon,' a novel framework where two competing models act as each other's evaluators (graders).
The competitive setup forces models to improve the quality of their reasoning trace, not just the final output.

stories.title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
stories.author: Lu Yin
bullet_points: DiaLLM addresses the 'robustness-generation gap' where LLMs understand dialects but fail to generate them.
The research involves continually pretraining open-weight models on the International Corpus of English.
It compares various implicit/explicit post-training paradigms combined with different model alignment strategies.

stories.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
stories.author: Andrew Saxe
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training allows models to compose primitive skills into higher-level reasoning strategies.
The study uses a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment, allowing for auditing of generated rewrite chains.
A Transformer model, pretrained on symbol-rewrite chains and post-trained with binary reward, successfully solves held-out reasoning problems.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a new paradigm for Limited Memory Language Models (LMLMs).
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in model weights.
CO-LMLM uses continuous keys in the KB to allow for continuous knowledge querying during generation.

stories.title: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay for Sample-Efficient Diffusion RLHF
stories.author: Soumik Mukhopadhyay
bullet_points: Addresses the sample inefficiency bottleneck in applying Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) to diffusion models.
Proposes two complementary strategies: Selective Timestep Weighting and Advantage-Based Replay.
Aims to make diffusion RLHF more practical by reducing the reliance on large amounts of human or reward model evaluations.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current Reinforcement Learning (RL) reasoning models where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but not necessarily better reasoning.
Introduces 'Agon,' a novel framework where two competing models act as each other's evaluators or 'graders.'
The competitive setup forces models to improve the quality of their reasoning trace, not just the final output, by having one model critique the other's solution.

stories.title: ECGLight: Compute-Light Framework For Paper ECG Digitization and Myocardial Infarction Screening
stories.author: Diego Paez-Granados
bullet_points: ECGLight is a new framework designed to digitize and analyze paper ECG printouts.
It addresses the challenge of limited computational capacity and connectivity in remote clinics.
The goal is to enable AI-based decision support for cardiovascular disease screening using physical ECGs.

stories.title: How Data Shapes RoPE Frequency Usage: From Positional Scale Matching to Length Generalization
stories.author: Ali Jadbabaie
bullet_points: The research investigates the non-uniform usage of Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) in transformer models.
It proposes a data-centered explanation: RoPE frequencies are selected to align with the relative-distance structure present in the training data.
The study formalizes a 'field-resolution tradeoff' related to the width ($W$) of the data-induced dependency profile.

stories.title: Max Out GRPO Signal: Adaptive Trace Prefix Control for Hard Reasoning Problems
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical issue in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) where hard examples fail to provide useful gradients.
The proposed method, AdaPrefix-GRPO, introduces an adaptive trace prefix control mechanism to manage problem difficulty during training.
This technique dynamically adjusts the difficulty (prefix length) based on training feedback, allowing the model to learn effectively from challenging frontier examples.

stories.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
stories.author: Yoav Artzi
bullet_points: Introduces Co-LMLM, a Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Model paradigm.
LMLMs externalize factual knowledge to a Knowledge Base (KB) instead of memorizing it in weights.
CO-LMLM uses continuous keys to pair with textual knowledge values for retrieval during generation.

stories.title: From Noisy Traces to Root Causes: Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction for Agent Optimization
stories.author: Yuqing Yang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of optimizing long-horizon AI agents that use LLMs for self-reflection and failure diagnosis.
Current methods struggle because real execution traces are redundant, heterogeneous, and contain irrelevant steps, leading to inefficient optimization.
The proposed solution involves 'Structural Trajectory Analysis and Causal Extraction' to move from noisy traces to identifying root causes for agent improvement.

stories.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
stories.author: Vladislav Beliaev
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agon,' a novel framework for competitive cross-model Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses a limitation in current reasoning models where only the final answer is graded, leading to verbose but not necessarily better reasoning.
Agon uses two competing models where one drafts a solution and the other acts as a grader/solver, providing implicit rival grading.

stories.title: Does Bielik Know What It Doesn't Know? Activation Dispersion Separates Entity Familiarity from Factual Reliability Across Model Scale
stories.author: Grzegorz Brzezinka
bullet_points: The research investigates if internal model activations can predict an LLM's familiarity with an entity before generating an answer.
The study uses Polish Bielik models across various scales (1.5B-11B) to test this hypothesis across different entity types (athletes, cities, etc.).
Findings suggest that entity familiarity, detectable via activations, correlates with the factual reliability of the model's output, especially for unseen entities.

stories.title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
stories.author: Lu Yin
bullet_points: DiaLLM addresses the 'Robustness-Generation Gap' where LLMs understand dialects but fail to generate them.
The research involves continually pretraining open-weight models on the International Corpus of English.
The study compares various implicit/explicit post-training paradigms combined with model alignment strategies.

stories.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
stories.author: Andrew Saxe
bullet_points: The research investigates whether Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training can enable models to compose primitive skills into higher-level reasoning strategies.
The study uses a controlled, fully observable rewrite-grammar environment to audit the model's generated reasoning steps.
A Transformer model pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains was post-trained with a binary reward on a Trace-based reasoning task, achieving success on held-out problems.

stories.title: Future Confidence Distillation in Large Language Models
stories.author: Sahil Kale
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for reliable confidence estimation in Large Language Models (LLMs) for deployment in confidence-aware systems.
Current methods often assess confidence only after the response is complete, failing to capture the dynamic nature of confidence during the generation process.
The research proposes investigating confidence from a temporal perspective to improve how LLMs estimate answer reliability throughout computation.

stories.title: GPT-5.6
stories.author: logickkk1
bullet_points: The news pertains to a potential release or update of a model named GPT-5.6 from OpenAI.
The content links directly to a PDF document on OpenAI's deployment safety page.
It also provides a link to the official documentation for the latest OpenAI API model.

stories.title: Announcing TypeScript 7.0
stories.author: devblogs.microsoft.com via evert
bullet_points: TypeScript 7.0 has been officially announced.
The announcement is shared on the Lobsters forum.
This represents a significant update to the TypeScript language ecosystem.

stories.title: An alternative to LLM quality gates: deterministic routing + sampling
stories.author: zxpmail
bullet_points: Challenges the fundamental assumption that LLMs can reliably judge the quality of other LLM outputs.
Proposes 'deterministic routing + sampling' as an alternative mechanism to traditional LLM quality gates.
Addresses a critical weakness in current LLM-based evaluation and validation pipelines.

stories.title: AI Governance for Engineering Teams
stories.author: hadil
bullet_points: Focuses on practical AI governance implementation for engineering teams.
Addresses critical operational aspects like guardrails, budgeting, and audit logging.
Targets the challenge of scaling governance practices in real-world engineering environments.

stories.title: AI Agent Checkout in Magento 2: Claude Places a Real Order via MCP
stories.author: angeo
bullet_points: Demonstrates an AI agent successfully completing a full guest checkout process in Magento 2.
The implementation utilizes a custom Magento 2 MCP server, avoiding traditional browser automation.
The article addresses the technical challenges involved, specifically mentioning the payment integration hurdle.

stories.title: Why Cursor Keeps Writing Command Injection Into Your Code (CWE-78)
stories.author: c_k_fb750e731394
bullet_points: The article discusses a security vulnerability (Command Injection, CWE-78) being introduced by AI code editors like Cursor.
The issue stems from AI models favoring common patterns, such as using exec() with template strings, often seen in tutorials.
This highlights a critical security risk associated with the current implementation and reliance on AI-generated code.
